commit.message:
fix(updater): download only changed files and remove retired ones

The GitHub updater had never been tested. Run against a real 0.5.4
install and GitHub, it had these faults:

- It downloaded the whole repository as a 48 MB zip and copied it over
  the installation, but never deleted anything. Updating 0.5.4 left 81
  removed or moved files behind, including old launcher definitions
  and the maintenance items, and the client loads every .wpn and .item
  it finds.
- It ignored copy failures, deleted the download anyway and restarted
  the game on a half-updated installation.
- A source install restarted NVGT with the path to "Infinite
  Warfare.nvgt" unquoted; the space split it and the game never came
  back.
- It judged the installed version by version.txt, so new files without
  a rebuilt executable looked like a finished update.
- It waited a fixed 1.5 s for the game to release its files, and in a
  release folder it would have added the whole source tree.

New updater/iw-update.ps1, run by the game after it exits:
- Pins the branch to one commit and reads its tree from the GitHub API.
  It compares every file by git blob SHA-1 (CRLF copies count as equal)
  and downloads only what differs from raw.githubusercontent.com. More
  than 150 changes, or a truncated tree, use the commit's zip instead.
- Verifies every download before touching the installation, backs up
  everything it replaces or deletes, and restores it all on any
  failure. It waits up to 30 s for locked files.
- Deletes files listed in updater/retired_files.txt, and files it
  installed last time that are gone now (updater/installed_files.txt).
- Never touches iwserver/admins.txt, motd.svr or currentmap.txt. Maps
  a release folder's layout: only the exe, documents, lib/, updater/
  and the client's content/ folders.
- Writes updater/last_update.txt and last_update.log, then restarts the
  game with a quoted path.
- Targets Windows PowerShell 5.1: User-Agent goes in -UserAgent, since
  5.1 refuses it in -Headers.

Client (updater.nvgt, Infinite Warfare.nvgt, release_tools.nvgt):
- cfu() compares GitHub's version.txt with version_name, then launches
  the script with -Root, -Restart, -Mode, -Repository and -Branch.
- updater_remove_retired_files() runs once per build, before content
  loads, so leftovers from the legacy updater are cleaned up.
- updater_report_last_result() announces the result on start.
- Release builds copy updater/iw-update.ps1 and retired_files.txt.

tools/update_retired_files.py writes the retired list from the full
history: deleted game-folder paths that do not exist now, never runtime
data or the old source/ snapshot. Run it after deleting or moving a
shipped file.

tools/tests/updater_regression.py serves this working tree through a
local stand-in for GitHub's API, raw and archive URLs. It checks five
updates:
- 0.5.4 to now: the result is identical, retired files are gone and
  admins.txt is kept.
- A two-file edit downloads exactly two files.
- An up-to-date install reports current.
- A failed download changes nothing.
- A release folder updates in place.
Disabling deletion, CRLF tolerance or protection each makes it fail. It
needs pwsh; only its static checks run without it.

Not compiled here: NVGT is not available. The script was run under
PowerShell 7.4 on Linux, against this test and the real GitHub, but not
under Windows PowerShell 5.1. No protocol, save or sound-pack change.

chore(release): raise the version to 0.5.8, build 99

Client version 0.58 ("0.5.8"), build 99, dated 2026-10-06, and
version.txt to match, so a 0.5.4 to 0.5.7 install sees an update to
test the rebuilt updater with. changes.txt gains the 0.5.8 entry for
the updater. The server's minimum client version stays 0.57: nothing
in the protocol changed.

Rebuild the client executable with C:/nvgt/nvgt.exe -c; it was not
rebuilt here, so the tracked Infinite Warfare.exe is still older.
